subject: Science
source: El-Moasser Science Main Book 2027 + Assessments + Final Revision + Final Exams

questions.text: A natural rock that attracts certain metallic objects is called a natural ______.
questions.answer: magnet

questions.text: The region surrounding a magnet where magnetic force appears is the magnetic ______.
questions.answer: field

questions.text: Imaginary lines representing magnetic force are called magnetic field ______.
questions.answer: lines

questions.text: Like magnetic poles repel each other and unlike poles attract each other.
questions.answer: True

questions.text: Which is a magnetic material?
questions.answer: Iron

questions.text: Which is non-magnetic?
questions.answer: Copper

questions.text: Give a reason: Iron and cobalt are magnetic materials.
questions.answer: Because they are attracted to a magnet.

questions.text: Give a reason: Not all metals are magnetic materials.
questions.answer: Some metals such as copper, gold and silver are not attracted to a magnet.

questions.text: Give a reason: Iron filings are denser near the poles of a magnet.
questions.answer: Because the magnetic field is strongest at the poles.

questions.text: Give a reason: A freely suspended magnet settles in a certain direction.
questions.answer: Earth acts like a giant magnet, so the magnet aligns with Earth's magnetic field.

questions.text: Give a reason: A compass box is not made of iron.
questions.answer: Iron would interact with the compass magnetic needle and affect its movement.

questions.text: Compare magnetic and non-magnetic materials.
questions.answer: Magnetic materials are attracted to a magnet, such as iron, cobalt and nickel; non-magnetic materials are not, such as copper, silver and aluminum.

questions.text: Compare electric field and magnetic field.
questions.answer: Electric field surrounds an electric charge; magnetic field surrounds a magnet. Both are represented by imaginary field lines.

questions.text: Compare electric field lines and magnetic field lines.
questions.answer: Both are imaginary and do not intersect; electric lines start at positive and end at negative charges, while magnetic lines start from the north pole and end at the south pole outside a magnet.

questions.text: Which is NOT one of the artificial magnet shapes studied?
questions.answer: Triangular magnet

questions.text: A single magnet is divided into several parts. What happens to each part?
questions.answer: Each part becomes a smaller magnet with both north and south poles.

questions.text: A magnet is brought near a mixture of copper filings, iron filings and sand. Which part is attracted?
questions.answer: Only the iron filings.

questions.text: Give a reason: A magnetic brush can reveal unclear fingerprints.
questions.answer: Iron filings stick to the traces left by fingerprints, making them visible.

questions.text: Two adjacent poles repel. What can you infer about the poles?
questions.answer: They are like poles (both north or both south).

questions.text: Two adjacent poles attract. What can you infer?
questions.answer: They are unlike poles.

questions.text: Magnetic field lines are most dense near the magnet poles.
questions.answer: True

questions.text: A magnet can have an isolated north pole after being cut.
questions.answer: False

questions.text: A compass is used mainly to determine:
questions.answer: geographical directions

questions.text: Consultant-generated application: A compass needle does not deflect near a metal sample. Can you conclude the sample is definitely non-magnetic?
questions.answer: Not from one observation alone; repeat under proper conditions, but absence of attraction/deflection suggests it may be non-magnetic.
